title: Six expressions to multiply: which method fits each?
description: Six expressions are multiplied out, some by the distributive property and some by an identity. The board puts two of the answers back with a test number.
teaching_notes: One idea: spot a square or a sum times a take away and use the identity, otherwise multiply every term by every term. Watch for students who drop a sign when a minus sign sits outside the bracket, or who forget the middle term of a square.

source: Figure it Out (identities and patterns, question 2)
video_script.why: The child can mend a wrong expansion, but has not yet chosen between an identity and the distributive property for six new expressions.
video_script.substitution: For each item, use an identity when it is a square or a sum times a take away, and otherwise multiply every term by every term, as the cards in the book did.
video_script.anchor: the six expressions of the book's question, each waiting for a method
video_script.payoff_line: The last item is twenty one p squared r plus forty two p r.

final_answer.spoken: twenty one p squared r plus forty two p r

video_script.design: One idea: choose the identity for a square or a sum times a take away, otherwise multiply every term by every term. The rule cards stay on the stage. The last item is left unworked until the answer.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; six expression cards in two rows: (p - 1)(p + 11), (3a - 9b)(3a + 9b), -(2y + 5)(3y + 4), (6x + 5y)², (2x - 1/2)², (7p) × (3r) × (p + 2)

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='six'/>It gives six expressions to multiply out.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which ones can use an identity, and which need the distributive property?

beats.on_screen: the six expression cards stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three rule cards: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b², (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b²; under them, the words Multiply every term by every term

marks.every: the words Multiply every term by every term appear
marks.rules: the three rule cards appear beside them

beats.colours: the three terms of each rule in three colours
narration: <bookmark mark='every'/>Your book allows the distributive property, which multiplies every term by every term.
<bookmark mark='rules'/>The identities are shortcuts for a square, and for a sum times a take away.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the six expressions from your book.

beats.on_screen: To find: each expression multiplied out

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to multiply out each expression.

marks.two: (ii) is marked as a sum times a take away

beats.colours: the like terms in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, item one. Multiply every term by every term, to get p squared plus eleven p minus p minus eleven.
<bookmark mark='one2'/>Eleven p minus p is ten p, so the item is p squared plus ten p minus eleven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Item two is a sum times a take away.
<bookmark mark='two2'/>Square each part to get nine eigh squared minus eighty one b squared.

marks.three2: the minus sign outside changes every sign: -6y² - 23y - 20
marks.four: (iv) is marked as the square of a sum

beats.colours: the three terms in three colours
narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, item three. First multiply the two brackets, to get six y squared plus twenty three y plus twenty.
<bookmark mark='three2'/>The minus sign outside changes every sign, giving minus six y squared minus twenty three y minus twenty.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Item four is the square of a sum.
<bookmark mark='four2'/>It is thirty six x squared, plus twice six x times five y, plus twenty five y squared. The middle part is sixty x y.

marks.five: (v) is marked as the square of a take away
marks.six2: 21pr × (p + 2) is written, not yet worked out

beats.colours: the three terms in three colours
narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, item five is the square of a take away.
<bookmark mark='five2'/>Two x squared is four x squared. Twice two x times one half is two x. One half squared is one quarter.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Item six. Seven p times three r is twenty one p r.
<bookmark mark='six2'/>Then multiply twenty one p r by p plus two.

beats.on_screen: Check item (i) with p = 2: (1)(13) = 13 and 4 + 20 - 11 = 13. Check item (iv) with x = 1, y = 1: 11² = 121 and 36 + 60 + 25 = 121

marks.one: p = 2 is chosen, and (2 - 1)(2 + 11) = 13 is written
marks.four: x = 1 and y = 1 are chosen, and (6 + 5)² = 121 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, put answers back in the question, with a test number. For item one, take p as two. One times thirteen is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='one2'/>Four plus twenty minus eleven is also thirteen.
<bookmark mark='four'/>For item four, take x and y as one. Eleven squared is one hundred twenty one.
<bookmark mark='four2'/>Thirty six plus sixty plus twenty five is also one hundred twenty one.

marks.list1: the first two answers are written in a column
marks.list3: the fourth and fifth answers are written, and the column is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last item is twenty one p squared r plus forty two p r.
<bookmark mark='list1'/>Item one is p squared plus ten p minus eleven. Item two is nine eigh squared minus eighty one b squared.
<bookmark mark='list2'/>Item three is minus six y squared minus twenty three y minus twenty.
<bookmark mark='list3'/>Item four is thirty six x squared plus sixty x y plus twenty five y squared. Item five is four x squared minus two x plus one quarter.
